hero.headline: Building a future through education.
hero.description: Ayaa South Sudanese Organization is a nonprofit organization headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky, dedicated to raising funds, resources and community support for Ayaa Senior Secondary School in Magwi County, South Sudan.
hero.cardHeading: Education is the foundation. Community is the force.

story.quote: The goal is bigger than a building. It is about giving the next generation a place to learn, grow, and imagine what comes next.
story.paragraph1: Simon Ottaviano survived war from South Sudan, eventually finding his way to United States of America, where he served in the United States Army, built his career and decided to give back to the community!
story.paragraph2: In 2021, with his wife's full support, he sold their family home and cashed out his entire 401(k) retirement savings — and used every dollar to build a school back in Magwi County, naming it after his mother, Ayaa.
story.paragraph3: Ayaa Senior Secondary School opened in 2022 and today serves over 600 students across Senior One through Senior Four. Ayaa South Sudanese Organization — based in Louisville, Kentucky — exists to raise the funds and support that keep it running and growing.

founder.name: Simon Ottaviano
founder.role: Founder & Director — Ayaa South Sudanese Organization, Louisville, KY
founder.bio: U.S. Army veteran. Real estate professional in Louisville, Kentucky. And the man who sold his house and his retirement to give the children of Magwi County a school. Simon's journey is one of the most remarkable stories of still being written. Ayaa Secondary School was name after his late Mother, Andreyina Ayaa Ottaviano.

impact.title: Simon sells everything
impact.desc: Simon and his wife sell their family home and cash out their 401(k) retirement savings to fund construction of a school in Magwi County.

impact.title: Ayaa opens its doors
impact.desc: Ayaa Senior Secondary School opens to great celebration in Magwi County, welcoming its first students to Senior One through Senior Four.

impact.title: Safe water arrives
impact.desc: WaterStep partners with Ayaa to install a clean-water system, ending the school's reliance on unsafe river water and expensive tanker deliveries.

impact.title: Students enrolled today
impact.desc: Over 600+ young people from Magwi County now attend Ayaa — studying, growing, and building toward their futures.

sections.storyDesc: From a refugee in IFO refugee camp Garissa District, Kenya to the United States, US Army Veteran and back home to built Ayaa Senior Secondary School. A journey of resilience, services, education, and giving back to the community.

watch.title: "South Sudanese Man Endured War to Bring Hope Home"
watch.description: This film follows Simon Ottaviano's journey — from the Lost Boys of Sudan to Louisville, Kentucky, to the construction of Ayaa Senior Secondary School in South Sudan. It also documents the safe-water project WaterStep brought to the school in 2023.

projects.title: Library/Boys' Dormitory
projects.desc: Most boys at Ayaa travel long distances on dangerous roads every day. A dormitory would give ~100 boys a safe, clean place to sleep and focus fully on their studies.

projects.title: Library, Active Fundraiser!
projects.desc: A dedicated library would give students greater access to books, study resources, and independent learning — critical for academic growth beyond the classroom.

projects.title: Water & Sanitation
projects.desc: Continue expanding and maintaining the clean-water infrastructure WaterStep helped establish — ensuring every student has access to safe water every day.
